title: Minimum Operations to Collect Elements
summary: Given an array of positive integers and an integer k, determine the least number of operations required to collect elements 1 through k by removing the last element of the array in each operation.
statement: Given an array of positive integers and an integer k, determine the least number of operations required to collect elements 1 through k by removing the last element of the array in each operation.
constraints: One operation removes the final element of nums.
Continue until every integer from one through k has been removed at least once.
Return the number of removals required; the input guarantees all required values occur.
hints: Track the required values not yet encountered.
Traverse nums backward because removal always comes from the end.
Discard each removed value from the required set and stop when it becomes empty.
The first empty-set moment is exactly the shortest suffix containing every value one through k.
editorial: The first empty-set moment is exactly the shortest suffix containing every value one through k.

tests.explanation: Removing 2,4,5,1 takes four operations and has then collected one and two.
All five removals are needed to see every value one through five.
